name: Milwaukee by Night: Politics of the Council (Lore)

text.content:
When the ancient @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} Hrothulf held the Princedom, he created a Council of Elders (one seat per Clan) to help administer the city and lend his rule broader legitimacy; when Hrothulf abdicated, the Council declared itself sovereign, tasked with keeping the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} out and the Anarchs in check. The Council now fights as often with the Prince as beside him, and pitting councilors against one another is a favored Elder tactic. Six of the original seven seats remain filled — the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} seat, once held by the reclusive Mark Decker, was removed after he stopped attending, and every attempt to restore it has failed amid clan rivalry over who would gain the extra vote. With six sitting members, ties are common, and breaking a Council deadlock has become an informal, semi-official duty of whoever holds the Princedom.

Following Psychomachia (the previous Prince's death, engineered by his own madness and ultimately ended by an adventuring coterie called "the Mask"), Milwaukee has no Prince, and the struggle to fill the throne has become the city's central political drama. Candidates and kingmakers include Gracis Nostinus (widely seen as the most capable claimant), Carna (seen by Edward Scott as an acceptably uncontroversial choice), and the retired former Prince Hrothulf (whom Scott would prefer restored to the throne, though Gracis would block it and Hrothulf shows no interest in returning to power).

Milwaukee is unusual in that virtually every faction of the Jyhad has a stake in its fate at once: two ancient rivals (Gracis Nostinus and Hrothulf) duel over a centuries-old betrayal; Council members jockey for the vacant throne; the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}'s agent Parovich schemes toward the city's collapse from within while his own fugitive childer plot his exposure; a magical "null zone" draws both powerful @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} elders and ravenous Werewolves; a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} (Lucina) dreams of elevating her Clan's standing; and the insane @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} Jacob/Esau wages a private, decades-long war against himself through unwitting pawns. The Lupine and the Sabbat both watch for any sign of weakness that would let them seize the city outright, and the Society of Leopold's Inquisition has begun quietly turning its attention to Milwaukee as well, hoping to exploit any breach in the Masquerade caused by the chaos.

Common tools of the city's political war include open violence (rare, and destabilizing), assassination (via the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} Badr-al-Budur, at steep cost, or via mortal killers like Victor), extortion and blackmail, and the Discipline-driven tactics of Dominate, Presence, and the Blood Bond — used both to neutralize dangerous rivals without an open kill and to build durable political followings.

pages.name: Brujah of Milwaukee: Scott and Akawa

text.content:
The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} hold one Council seat, occupied by Sir Edward Scott, who prioritizes shielding the city's Anarchs from Elder prejudice above all else and is regarded by his fellow councilors as "just another Anarch" despite his five centuries of unlife. Scott opposes restoring the seventh Council seat unless it goes to a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel}, opposes a violent succession war, and has used "vote extortion" — challenging fellow councilors to duels to sway their votes — as an accepted, if distasteful, Milwaukee political tradition.

Scott's fiercest rival is his own unknowing childe, Akawa, leader of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.hs33xrNXWT2UXXS4]{Blood Brothers} gang; the two duel constantly and hate each other for different reasons (Scott resents Akawa's challenge to his Anarch leadership, while Akawa secretly resents Scott as the sire who does not remember him). Despite this, both men are quietly loyal to the broader Anarch cause and would each prefer to see the other's faction, if not the other personally, prosper. The Brujah scattered through the Anarch gangs beyond Scott and Akawa are numerous but poorly organized, and could be swayed to any side with the right incentive.

pages.name: Mark Decker and the Anubi's Political Leverage

text.content: Mark Decker refuses, on principle, to involve himself or his Anubi in Council politics, having grown to despise a Council that dismissed his repeated warnings about Lupine attacks as "the ravings of an arrogant lunatic" — even after a Werewolf raid at the turn of the century proved him right. He will not ally with anyone who does not offer him substantial, concrete help against the Lupine, and no faction save the player-facing "Mask" is likely to make such an offer unprompted. Should he choose to engage, Decker holds enormous latent leverage: the Anubi is the single most dangerous fighting force in the city, and if it stopped patrolling, the Lupine would rapidly begin probing deeper into Milwaukee proper. Decker could also, in principle, blockade the Outlands entirely, sealing off all road access to the city and forcing any faction seeking outside reinforcements to either negotiate with him or fight through his patrols. He has no allies among the Council, who consider him a rogue madman possibly in league with the Lupine themselves.

vtmlarp.source: Milwaukee by Night, Chapter Four: Politics
